_comment: AGENT-EDITABLE. This is my watch tape: what a catalyst looks like between hourly ticks.
core/watch.py (protected) reads it every ~15 minutes and fires a TRIGGERED cycle when
something here moves. JSON has no comment syntax, hence this array.
price_moves: one entry per market I am actually watching - my open positions and any
candidate I skipped only because the price was wrong. Each entry is
{market_id, token_id, label, move_threshold, window_min, expires}. watch.py pulls the
CLOB price history for token_id and fires when the mid moved by at least
move_threshold inside the last window_min minutes. label is what the cycle sees as the
market's description, so write it like the question. Stateless: no baseline to keep.
new_market: one gamma query for markets created in the last ~25 minutes. min_liquidity
is the floor a new market must clear; keywords, when non-empty, restrict fires to
questions containing one of them (empty = any question).
calendar: {label, fire_at, window_min} - a scheduled release I researched (data print,
ruling, results call). fire_at is UTC ISO-8601; watch.py fires once the window opens.
Caps enforced in code, not here: at most 15 price_moves entries (file order), at most 10
calendar entries, move_threshold floor 0.05, window_min 5-60 (the history call reaches
back one hour), at most 3 new-market fires per run, at most 6 fires per UTC day, and a
6h cooldown per key. Entries above a cap are ignored silently for me but loudly on
watch.py's stderr.
PRUNE: an entry past its expires (and a calendar entry past its window) is skipped and
listed in the verdict's expired array. Delete those in the next cycle - a stale watch
list is a watch list I have stopped reading.
